exposure: prenatal ambient air pollution (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, nitrogen oxides, elemental carbon, organic carbon, sulfur dioxide, ozone, sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, secondary organic aerosols, sea salt)
postnatal ambient air pollution (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, nitrogen oxides, elemental carbon, organic carbon, sulfur dioxide, ozone, sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, secondary organic aerosols, sea salt)
cohort: The study included 1,060,154 live-born singletons born in Denmark between 1998 and 2016.
finding: Early-life exposure to ambient air pollution from multiple sources, both pre- and postnatally, significantly contributes to the development of asthma in children aged 0-19 years.
